extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and institutional staff preparing NIH grant applications (investigators, administrators, mentors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exemplar materials for drafting and assembling NIH grant applications and related attachments (biosketches, plans, forms, progress reports). Includes pointers to sample funded applications, templates, and topic-specific format pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure Compliance with Current Application Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure Compliance with Current Application Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applications below used the form version and instructions that were in effect at the time of their submission. Forms and instructions change regularly. Read and carefully follow the instructions in your chosen funding opportunity and the How to Apply – Application Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Instructions in Your Chosen Funding Opportunity and How-to Guide
rubrics_metrics.description: Read and carefully follow the instructions in your chosen funding opportunity and the How to Apply – Application Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume samples reflect current required forms or page limits; adapt to the current FOA and application guide. Your chosen approach must follow the instructions in your funding opportunity and the How to Apply – Application Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Sample Applications and Documents as Demonstrations, Not Prescriptive Templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples can be helpful as a demonstration of effective ways to present information but may not be the best or current way to present your science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The best way to present your science may differ substantially from the approaches shown here. Samples are not available for all grant programs; when using samples, keep in mind form/instruction changes and program differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Feedback on Your Draft Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek feedback on your draft application from mentors and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mentors, colleagues, and institutional staff to review drafts; samples are only illustrative and external feedback helps tailor presentation and correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Correct Formats and Templates for Required Attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use NIH-provided format pages and templates for specific attachments (e.g., Biographical Sketch Common Form, Current and Pending (Other) Support, Data Management and Sharing plans, fellowship/training data tables, additional senior/key persons, additional performance sites).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access the Application Format Pages for the exact formats required for each attachment type; use provided templates to ensure compliance with formatting and content expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare Complete and Compliant Biosketches
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide biosketch(es) using the NIH Biographical Sketch format appropriate for the activity (fellowship vs. non-fellowship) and follow instructions and sample language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Biosketch Format Pages, Instructions, and Samples to ensure required sections and formatting elements are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose Other Support Clearly and Accurately
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Other Support and related documentation per NIH format and instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Other Support Format Page and samples to ensure complete disclosure of financial and other support that may be relevant to the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate Research Intent and Public Health Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Write clear application titles, abstracts, and public health relevance statements that communicate research intent and value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'Application Titles, Abstracts, and Public Health Relevance Statements: Communicating Research Intent and Value' for examples and suggested language to convey the significance and intended impact of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate Scientific Rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Address scientific rigor in the application as required by NIH policies (methods, experimental design, reproducibility considerations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the NIH Scientific Rigor resources and sample language to describe how rigor, reproducibility, and valid experimental design are built into the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare Required Topic-Specific Plans (DMS, Authentication, Model Organism Sharing, Multiple PI Plans)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include topic-specific plans when applicable: Data Management and Sharing (DMS) plan, Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources Plans, Model Organism Sharing Plans, Multiple Principal Investigators/Project Leadership Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided sample plans and format pages to ensure required content and formatting for each plan type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with Animal Welfare Documentation (OLAW)
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, provide animal documents (welfare assurances, checklists, study proposals) per Office of Laboratory Animal Welfare (OLAW) guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Animal Documents section for OLAW-specific templates and required elements for animal research assurances and proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Rules for Allowable Appendix Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Only include appendix materials that are allowable under NIH rules and follow the specified formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the 'Allowable Appendix Materials' resource to know what may be appended and how to format such materials to avoid noncompliance or administrative rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Correct Submission Methods and Forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Access fillable forms via the Submission Options and use the prescribed system (e.g., ASSIST) or mechanisms required for your opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To access fillable forms for your opportunity, you must use one of the Submission Options. Follow system-specific instructions for assembling and submitting the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare Accurate Budgeting and Person-Month Calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate and report person months and other budget elements accurately per NIH instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the 'Person Months FAQ on Calculations' for guidance on how to compute and report person months and related budget components correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide Complete Progress Reporting and Project Outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: For progress reports (RPPR) and multi-year funded awards, prepare clear project outcomes and comply with RPPR instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 'Project Outcomes for Research Performance Progress Report (RPPR)' resource to structure outcome reporting and meet reporting requirements.
